skill.description: Guides agents through Azure Developer CLI setup for Azure Container Apps, including azure.yaml, Bicep infrastructure, remote ACR builds, environment flow, and deployment troubleshooting.

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily Azure deployment documentation, and most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, example URLs, .azure paths, and /dev/null redirection. The confirmed issues are predictable temporary-file use in a sample hook and a command that can expose all azd environment values. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary file path in deployment hook
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or an azd-scoped private directory for saved domain data, quote the path, and remove it with a cleanup trap.

remediation.issue: Full azd environment dump can reveal secrets
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad environment-dump guidance with targeted checks and require redaction before sharing command output.
Add guidance to verify subscription, resource group, environment name, and user approval before deployment or RBAC commands.

content.user_title: Deploy Azure Container Apps with azd
content.value_statement: Azure Container Apps deployments often require matching azd, Bicep, environment, and Docker settings. This skill gives agents practical patterns for azure.yaml, remote builds, managed identity, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Outline azure.yaml service definitions for frontend and backend Container Apps.
Map azd environment values into Bicep parameters and outputs.
Recommend remote container builds through Azure Container Registry.
Describe idempotent deployment patterns for existing resources and custom domains.
Show managed identity and RBAC patterns for Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search.
List common azd and Azure CLI commands for deployment and debugging.
limitations: Does not create a complete project repository by itself.
Requires valid Azure credentials, subscription access, and installed azd and Azure CLI tools.
Examples must be adapted for each resource group, service name, and region.
May cause cloud resource changes when commands are executed by an agent or user.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a Container Apps Project
use_cases.description: Create the azd structure, service definitions, and Bicep entry points for a new containerized application.

use_cases.title: Add Remote Build Deployment
use_cases.description: Configure Docker build context and remoteBuild settings so images build in Azure Container Registry.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Failed azd Deployments
use_cases.description: Review environment variables, service tags, logs, and Bicep outputs when azd up or azd deploy fails.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic azd Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a minimal azd project for one backend service on Azure Container Apps. Include the required files and explain each step.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Frontend and Backend Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my azd configuration for a frontend and backend deployed to Azure Container Apps. Use remote builds and internal backend routing.

prompt_templates.title: Add Managed Identity Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Bicep and azd hooks that give my backend managed identity access to Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search. Avoid broad roles.

prompt_templates.title: Make Redeployments Idempotent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Container Apps deployment approach for idempotency. Preserve existing resources, custom domains, Bicep outputs, and azd environment values.

output_examples.input: I need a first azd deployment plan for a Python API.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step setup checklist covering project layout, service settings, infrastructure files, environment creation, and deployment verification.

output_examples.input: My frontend cannot reach the backend after deployment.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks internal service DNS, container app environment, proxy configuration, and backend URI output values.

output_examples.input: I need managed identity access to Azure OpenAI.
output_examples.output: A least-privilege RBAC plan that identifies the backend principal, target resource scope, role choice, and verification steps.

best_practices: Confirm the Azure subscription, tenant, and environment name before running deployment or RBAC commands.
Use remote builds for container images and keep Docker contexts small.
Store secrets through azd environment management and redact values before sharing logs.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample resource names, scopes, or regions into production without review.
Do not print full environment values in shared transcripts or CI logs.
Do not ignore failed role assignments during secure deployment validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me deploy?
faq.answer: It helps deploy containerized frontend and backend services to Azure Container Apps with azd and Bicep.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides command patterns. Agents should request confirmation before executing deployment, logging, or RBAC commands.

faq.question: Can it manage secrets?
faq.answer: It explains azd environment flow, but secrets still need secure handling and redaction.

faq.question: Does it support multi-service apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes frontend, backend, internal routing, and service discovery patterns.

faq.question: What Azure tools are required?
faq.answer: You need Azure Developer CLI, Azure CLI, Docker project files, and permissions for the target subscription.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot azd up failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers environment values, Container Apps logs, Bicep outputs, and service tags.
